title: Free cocompletion by space-valued presheaves
statement:
Use the infinity categories and nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the coherent functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means $\mathcal U$-small, and $\mathcal S$ denotes the infinity category of small spaces. Let $D$ be a small infinity category. The infinity category $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ has small mapping spaces and admits all small colimits. Write $j:D\to\mathcal P(D)$ for $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. For every infinity category $\mathcal V$ in the larger universe admitting all small colimits, restriction along $j$ induces an equivalence of infinity categories
$$j^*:\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\mathcal P(D),\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal V),$$
where the left side is the full subcategory of coherent functors preserving small colimits. The equivalence includes natural transformations and their higher simplices, so an equivalence between the restrictions of two such functors lifts to a natural equivalence between those functors.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.4 and Theorem 5.1.5.6, printed pp. 318 and 327; the usual small-mapping-space convention for presheaves on a small infinity category Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: First control size and colimits. For $F,G\in\mathcal P(D)$ choose $\mathcal U$-small right fibrations $q_F:E_F\to D$ and $q_G:E_G\to D$ classifying them. Transport classification identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(F,G)$ with the Kan complex of simplicial maps $E_F\times\Delta^n\to E_G$ over $D$. Each degree of this complex is $\mathcal U$-small since both total spaces are small, so the mapping space has a small model. Small colimits exist in $\mathcal S$ by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. To obtain existence in $\mathcal P(D)$ explicitly, fix a small simplicial set $K$. A colimit cocone on $p:K\to\mathcal S$ is a universal arrow $p\to\Delta_K L$ by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply the opposite universal-arrow assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $\Delta_K:\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$: it assembles these arrows to a coherent left adjoint $\operatorname{colim}_K$, and supplies its adjunction also for coherent $D^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams. Currying by the simplicial identity $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times K\cong K\times D^{\mathrm{op}}$ turns the latter mapping-space adjunction into $\operatorname{colim}_K\dashv\Delta_K$ for $\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Its unit cocone is thus the required colimit, evaluated objectwise. This constructs every small colimit in $\mathcal P(D)$; the objectwise characterization of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies and detects its cocone. For later use put $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$ and let $\iota:\mathcal P(D)\to\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$ be universe inclusion. Its values preserve small colimit cocones by the new space lemma, so objectwise detection shows that $\iota$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits. The same right-fibration size argument in $\mathcal U'$ shows that $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$ has $\mathcal U'$-small mapping spaces. Form $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$ in one further auxiliary universe; this changes no hypothesis on $D$ or on the target $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Corollaries 5.1.2.3-4; Corollary 4.2.4.8; right-fibration classification of Section 3.3.2

proof.text: Record the sections calculation explicitly, rather than introducing another lemma. Let $B$ be a small quasicategory and let a right fibration $Z\to B$ classify $H:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ (the same calculation works in $\mathcal U'$). The constant terminal-space functor is classified by $B\to B$. Thus transport classification identifies the space of sections $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(B,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta *,H)$. The latter is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(*,\lim H)$ by the mapping-space universal property of the limit; limits of spaces exist by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Finally $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(*,L)\simeq L$, since a simplex of the simplicial mapping complex from a point to a Kan complex $L$ is just a simplex of $L$; [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies that enriched mapping complex with the mapping space of the coherent nerve presenting spaces. Hence sections are $\lim H$. These are the displayed classification and cone equivalences, so they are natural in $H$ and in pullbacks on $B$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.3.4 and its opposite; here derived from the cited classification and cone statements

proof.text:
For $F,G\in\mathcal P(D)$ a map $E_F\to E_G$ over $D$ is precisely a section of $E_F\times_D E_G\to E_F$, in every simplicial degree. Pullback compatibility of transport says that this right fibration classifies $G\circ q_F^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply step 2 to obtain the canonical equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(F,G)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}G(q_F(e)).$$
For a larger-valued presheaf $Q$, choose its right-fibration representative $E_Q\to D$ in $\mathcal U'$. By the right-fibration compatibility clause of [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe], the unchanged small right fibration $E_F\to D$, regarded in $\mathcal U'$, classifies $\iota F$. Classification in $\mathcal U'$ identifies the mapping space from $\iota F$ to $Q$ with maps $E_F\to E_Q$ over $D$. In each simplicial degree these are sections of $E_F\times_D E_Q\to E_F$; pullback classification gives its presheaf $Q\circ q_F^{\mathrm{op}}$, so step 2 identifies that section space with its limit. This gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota F,Q)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}Q(q_F(e))$$
for every $\mathcal U'$-space-valued presheaf $Q$. The displayed equivalences use the actual map-over-$D$ comparison and pullback, so they commute with precomposition in $F$ and postcomposition in $G$ or $Q$, including higher simplices.

source.place: Sections 3.3.2-3.3.3; maps of right fibrations as sections of a pullback

proof.text: Derive the canonical density cocone, not merely an unspecified presentation of $F$. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation], the right fibration $D\times_{\mathcal P(D)}\mathcal P(D)_{/F}\to D$ is classified by $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(j(d),F)\simeq F(d)$; the target-fixed slice classifier is supplied by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Consequently it is equivalent over $D$ to $E_F$. Its canonical arrows to $F$ give a coherent cocone $j q_F\to\Delta F$. For any test presheaf $G$, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{Map}(j(q_F(e)),G)$ with $G(q_F(e))$, and step 3 identifies the limit of these spaces with $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)$. These are the maps induced by that cocone: a transformation $\eta:F\to G$ sends an element $e=(d,x)$ to $\eta_d(x)$, which is evaluation at the identity of the composite $j(d)\xrightarrow{x}F\xrightarrow{\eta}G$. Thus the sections comparison of step 3 and the cocone comparison agree, including their higher simplices by the natural evaluation and transport equivalences. The colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] now shows that this cocone is colimiting. Evaluation at $G=j(d')$ also proves that $j$ is fully faithful. Let $A$ be its full essential image. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], $j:D\to A$ has a coherent quasi-inverse. Write $k:A\to D$ for that quasi-inverse and $\epsilon:jk\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$ for its counit. The functor from $A_{/F}$ to the pullback slice over $D$ sends $(a,u:a\to F)$ to $(k(a),u\epsilon_a:jk(a)\to F)$; in the other direction use $(d,x)\mapsto(j(d),x)$. The unit and counit, whiskered with these arrows, give the two inverse natural equivalences, on all simplices. Combining with the slice classifier identifies $A_{/F}$ with $E_F$, so $A_{/F}$ is essentially $\mathcal U$-small and its canonical cocone in $\mathcal P(D)$ is colimiting. Here equivalences of right-fibration classifiers give maps with inverse homotopies over $D$; these supply equivalences of their total categories. Reindexing a cone by a functor equivalence preserves its universal property, since restriction along the equivalence and its quasi-inverse are inverse on coherent cone spaces.

Fix $f:D\to\mathcal V$. Compose with a quasi-inverse of $D\simeq A$ to get $f_A:A\to\mathcal V$. For every $F$, write $a_F:A_{/F}\to A$ for the projection. The diagram $f_Aa_F$ admits a colimit: reindex it by its small model $E_F$ from step 4, and use the assumed small cocompleteness of $\mathcal V$. Explicitly, choose an equivalence $r:E_F\to A_{/F}$ and a quasi-inverse $t$. A colimit cocone for $f_Aa_Fr$ gives a cocone for $f_Aa_F$ by precomposition with $t$ and the equivalence $rt\simeq1$; restrictions along $r,t$ identify the two cocone spaces and their universal arrows. The opposite of the fixed-boundary assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] then gives a join cocone restricting exactly to $f_Aa_F$ on $A_{/F}$. These are the actual local lifts required below, not just choices of colimit apices. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] to $A\subseteq\mathcal P(D)$ and $p:\mathcal V\to *$. This is an isofibration: inner horns lift since $\mathcal V$ is a quasicategory and the identity edge lifts the unique equivalence of $*$. For this $p$, local $p$-colimit cocones are ordinary colimit cocones. To check the last assertion with the precise conventions of the cited lemma, apply the opposite of the join-cone mapping formula of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]: a map between two cocones is a boundary transformation, an apex map, and the path relating them. For a colimiting first cocone with apex $x$ and a test cocone with apex $y$, the universal-arrow map $\operatorname{Map}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}(f_Aa_F,\Delta y)$ is an equivalence. The mapping formula expresses the space of maps between these join cocones as its homotopy pullback along the map sending a boundary transformation $b$ to the composite of $b$ with the test cocone. Projection from this homotopy pullback to the space of boundary transformations is therefore an equivalence. This is exactly the homotopy-pullback square defining a $p$-colimit for $p$ to a point. The existence lemma therefore gives $H:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal V$, with $H|_A=f_A$ and with all these local cocones colimiting. In particular $Hj\simeq f$ and
$$H(F)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{e\in E_F}f(q_F(e)).$$
This is a coherent functor furnished by relative Kan existence; no functor is chosen from unrelated objectwise colimit choices.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(2), via Lemma 4.3.2.13; join/ordinary cocone comparison of Section 4.2

proof.text:
For $v\in\mathcal V$, form $Q_v:D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$, $Q_v(d)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(f(d),v)$. The coherent mapping bifunctor and precomposition action are supplied by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] with $\mathcal U'$ as the mapping-space universe. This is legitimate because $\mathcal V$ lies in $\mathcal U'$; its mapping spaces need not be $\mathcal U$-small. The colimit cocone from step 5 and the colimit mapping-space criterion give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(F),v)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(f(q_F(e)),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota F,Q_v),$$
where the second equivalence is step 3. More precisely this map takes $a:H(F)\to v$ to the transformation whose component at a point $x\in F(d)$ is $f(d)\xrightarrow{\sim}Hj(d)\xrightarrow{H(x)}H(F)\xrightarrow{a}v$, using Yoneda evaluation to regard $x$ as $j(d)\to F$. The coherent evaluation equivalence, $H$, and composition make this a natural transformation of the two mapping bifunctors. The preceding pointwise calculation proves that its components are equivalences, hence it is a coherent natural equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(1): mapping-space calculation for the colimit preservation direction

proof.text:
Prove that $H$ preserves every small colimit. Let $p:K\to\mathcal P(D)$ have colimit cocone with apex $L$, with $K$ any $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set. Step 1 says that $\iota L$ with the image cocone is the colimit of $\iota p$. Testing against $v\in\mathcal V$, step 6 and the mapping-space colimit criterion give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(L),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota L,Q_v)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota p(k),Q_v)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(p(k)),v).$$
Naturality from step 6 identifies this composite with precomposition by the cocone $Hp\to\Delta H(L)$. The same colimit criterion proves that this cocone is colimiting. Thus $H$ preserves small colimits, including the empty colimit; $K=\varnothing$ makes both limiting mapping spaces terminal. This proves essential surjectivity of the stated restriction functor for every permitted $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(1), expressed through the larger-space mapping presheaf; Theorem 5.1.5.6

proof.text:
Let $B_1,B_2:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal V$ preserve small colimits. The canonical cocone on $A_{/F}$ is the small colimit of step 4, so applying $B_1$ still gives a colimit for every $F$. The first hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] is therefore satisfied for $A\subseteq\mathcal P(D)$, $F=B_1$, $G=B_2$. It gives an equivalence on the mapping spaces between these functors and their restrictions to $A$. Restriction along $D\simeq A$ is also an equivalence on functor categories: precomposition with a quasi-inverse is its inverse, with the natural equivalences obtained by whiskering those of $D\simeq A$. Hence restriction along $j$ induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}(B_1,B_2)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B_1j,B_2j).$$
This is the actual restriction map, coherent under precomposition and postcomposition by the cited statement. Thus $j^*$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory of colimit-preserving functors.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2.12 and Corollary 4.3.2.16; colimit-preserving direction of Lemma 5.1.5.5(1)

proof.text: The source full subcategory and both functor categories are quasicategories in a sufficiently large auxiliary universe by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Steps 5-7 show that every target object $f$ is equivalent to $Hj$, and step 8 shows that $j^*$ is fully faithful. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to $j^*$; its full essential image is all of $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal V)$, so it has a coherent quasi-inverse. This is the claimed equivalence of infinity categories, retaining transformation spaces and their higher compositions. In particular an equivalence between two restrictions lifts to an equivalence upstairs: apply the quasi-inverse to that edge and compose with the quasi-inverse unit equivalences.
